walkthroughs.body_html: A hedonic scale rates liking, usually 1-5 or 1-9. "How much do you like the sweetness?" 5 = like extremely. Easy to use with non-trained tasters; results turn into average scores and bar charts.

Ranking tests put samples in order — "sweetest to least sweet". Paired comparison just asks which of two samples is preferred. Both are quick and produce clear results, but they don't say by how much.

A triangle test gives three coded samples: two identical, one different. Tasters identify the odd one. It tests whether two recipes are perceptibly different — useful when reducing sugar or salt in a product.
